verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. The test at login-callback.test.ts:121-134 declares (in its own comment) that it covers a rejection raised before anyone awaits waitForCallback, but the path it drives (/callback?code=unbound) hits login.ts:306-317, which only writes 400, warns once, and returns — it never calls callbackReject or sets `settled`. `callbackReject` is invoked in exactly one place, the 30s timeout at login.ts:373-385, which the test's 50ms settledWithin window plus the close() in finally guarantees is never reached. Therefore the guard the test exists to protect, `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` at login.ts:259, could be deleted with no effect on this test, and there is no unhandled-rejection listener/assertion anywhere in the test file to catch it either. The remaining assertions (400 status, promise unsettled) are an exact subset of the preceding test at lines 92-119, which drives the same request. This is fake coverage for a real behavior (the pre-await rejection guard is untested) — squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by impact.

I confirmed `startCallbackServer` is only ever constructed in packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts (repo-wide grep for `startCallbackServer` and for `wafflebase login|commands/login` finds no other test/e2e caller), and read that file in full: the nonce-less test (L92-119) asserts only the 400 response body (L100), the single warning (L103-104), non-settlement within 50ms (L105) and that the real callback still wins (L110-115). No test ever reaches the timeout. `Grep 'Login timed out'` repo-wide hits only login.ts:380 and docs prose, so neither timeout message is asserted anywhere. The timeout is hardcoded `30_000` and the options bag (login.ts:234) exposes only `allowUnbound`/`warn`, i.e. no clock or timeout injection; fake timers are used in packages/frontend, packages/slides and packages/backend but nowhere in packages/cli, so the branch is not reachable from the suite as written. This is the sole channel by which a real user learns about server version skew / --allow-unbound-callback, so it is a clear behavior change with no meaningful test — major under the missing-tests lane.

verdict.reason: The login action handler is never exercised by any test in the repository. The only importer of `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` in tests is `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts`, and its test at line 184 ("keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr") asserts only on `srv.startUrl` from `startCallbackServer` (line 190-191) and the `/start` 302 redirect (line 195-202) — it never runs the command action, never spies on `console.error`, and never observes `open`. The `registerLoginCommand` test (line 226-237) asserts only that the command and `--allow-unbound-callback` option exist. Therefore the stated guarantee implemented at login.ts:67 (`console.error(\`Opening browser: ${startUrl}\`)`) and login.ts:72 (`await open(startUrl)`) is untested: replacing either with `buildAuthorizeUrl(server, port, state)` leaves every assertion green. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: no test anywhere mocks/imports `open` (only login.ts:71 and a comment at login-callback.test.ts:122); no test matches `Opening browser`, `open(startUrl)`, or `--allow-unbound-callback` outside that file and docs; `parseAsync`-driven tests (tabs, read-dry-run, output, schema) never drive `login` — output.test.ts:500-516 only checks `login` appears in the command-name list; backend `auth/cli-auth.store.spec.ts` and `auth/auth.controller.spec.ts` cover the server leg, not the CLI hand-off. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a security-relevant behavior change shipped with a test that names the guarantee but cannot fail if the hand-off regresses.

finding.summary: The CLI half of the nonce feature — sending `cliState` in the OAuth URL — has no test at all
finding.evidence: The whole security property depends on `login`'s action appending `&cliState=${encodeURIComponent(state)}` (login.ts:71-73) and passing the same `state` to `startCallbackServer` (login.ts:58-64). The new suite `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` only imports `startCallbackServer`/`stateMatches`/`UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` and calls them directly with a nonce it mints itself; nothing imports `registerLoginCommand` or runs the action. If the `&cliState=` term were dropped (or the nonce passed to the server differed from the one in the URL), every test in the diff — CLI and backend — would still pass, while every real login would 400 with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the CLI-side `cliState` behavior has no test and that `registerLoginCommand` is never imported by any test. Both are false in this tree. `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:176-182` directly tests `buildAuthorizeUrl` (exported from login.ts:204-213), asserting the full URL string including `&cliState=a%20b%2Fc%2Bd` and that the param decodes back to the raw nonce — dropping the `&cliState=` term fails this test, contradicting "every test would still pass". `test/login-callback.test.ts:184-206` additionally runs a real callback server, sets the authorize URL, performs an actual `GET /start`, and asserts the 302 `Location` is the nonce-carrying authorize URL with `cliState === NONCE`. And `test/login-callback.test.ts:8` imports `registerLoginCommand`, with `test/login-callback.test.ts:226-237` registering it on a real Command and asserting the `--allow-unbound-callback` option. The reviewer's cited line numbers (login.ts:71-73, 58-64) also do not match the actual nonce code, indicating stale evidence. The only untested sliver is running the `.action()` body itself to prove the same local `state` variable feeds both calls on adjacent lines (login.ts:46-66), which does not amount to the claimed total absence of coverage.
